title: Cursor Changelog 2026: Upcoming AI-Powered Coding Enhancements

facts.fact: The $200/month Ultra plan for Cursor launched in June 2025, offering 20× more model usage.
The Ultra plan offers 20× more model usage than the base offering, per the blog.
facts.quote: Offering 20× more model usage and priority features

facts.fact: By mid-2025, over 50% of Fortune 500 companies had adopted Cursor, according to the blog.
facts.quote: By mid-2025, over 50% of Fortune 500 companies had adopted Cursor, including tech giants like Nvidia, Uber, and Adobe.

facts.fact: Cursor 0.50 (May 2025) introduced unified request-based pricing, replacing token-based models.
facts.quote: The update also brought unified request-based pricing, replacing the confusing token-based models that plagued early AI tools.

facts.fact: Cursor 0.50 introduced Background Agents that can execute tasks independently while developers work on other things.
Cursor 1.0 (June 2025) introduced BugBot, an automated PR code reviewer that catches issues before merge.
facts.quote: BugBot emerged as the standout feature, an automated PR code reviewer that catches issues before merge

facts.fact: Cursor 1.5 delivered a Linear integration allowing developers to launch Background Agents from issue tickets.
facts.quote: **Version 1.5** delivered the [Linear integration](https://cursor.com/changelog/1-5?ref=blog.promptlayer.com), allowing developers to launch Background Agents directly from issue tickets.

facts.fact: Cursor 1.6 introduced custom slash commands saved as reusable prompts in .cursor/commands/*.md files.
facts.quote: **Version 1.6** introduced [custom slash commands](https://cursor.com/changelog/1-6?ref=blog.promptlayer.com),reusable prompts saved in `.cursor/commands/*.md` files.

facts.fact: Cursor 1.7 introduced Hooks (beta), custom scripts to observe and control agent behavior at runtime.
facts.quote: Hooks (beta), custom scripts to observe and control agent behavior at runtime.

facts.fact: Cursor's Team Rules allow organizations to define global policies, including BugBot rules applied across all projects (Cursor 1.7).
facts.quote: Team Rules allowed organizations to define global policies, including BugBot rules applied across all projects.

facts.fact: Cursor's Max Mode is available for all top models using token-based pricing, per the 0.50 release notes summarized in the blog.
facts.quote: Max Mode available for all top models using token-based pricing

facts.fact: The blog states Anysphere has not published a formal 2026 roadmap for Cursor.
facts.quote: While Anysphere hasn't published a formal 2026 roadmap, the trajectory points clearly toward several key areas of development.

facts.fact: The blog states that Cursor has a valuation of nearly $10B (a third-party-style claim the author attributes to Cursor's position, not a verified figure).
facts.quote: With nearly $10B in valuation and partnerships with all major model providers

facts.fact: According to the blog, Cursor has millions of developers using it.
facts.quote: Cursor has proven that’s happening now, at scale, with millions of developers and over half the Fortune 500 already on board.

facts.fact: According to the blog, over half of the Fortune 500 companies have adopted Cursor.
facts.quote: with millions of developers and over half the Fortune 500 already on board.
